title: Balance Transfer Cards: When They're Worth It (Real Numbers)

lines.cap: A 0% balance transfer sounds like free money.
lines.say: A zero percent balance transfer sounds like free money.
Sometimes it is. Sometimes it's a trap. Let's run the numbers.

lines.cap: Our example: $5,000 on a card at 24%. About $100 of interest a month.
lines.say: Our example: five thousand dollars on a card at twenty-four percent. About a hundred dollars of interest a month.
Here's how a balance transfer works, when it's worth it, and how it goes wrong.
How it works.

items.t: Move the balance to a new card
0% for a promo period, often 12–21 months

lines.cap: You move the balance to a new card that charges 0% for a promo period, often 12 to 21 months. In exchange, you pay a one-time fee, often 3% to 5%. You'll usually need good credit to qualify.
lines.say: You move the balance to a new card that charges zero percent for a promo period, often twelve to twenty-one months. In exchange, you pay a one-time fee, often three to five percent. You'll usually need good credit to qualify.
At three percent, the fee on five thousand is a hundred fifty dollars.
When it's worth it.

lines.cap: Say the promo lasts 18 months. $5,150 divided by 18 is $287 a month. Pay that, and it's gone right as the promo ends.
lines.say: Say the promo lasts eighteen months. Fifty-one fifty, divided by eighteen, is two eighty-seven a month. Pay that, and it's gone right as the promo ends.

lines.cap: Stay on the 24% card, paying the same $287: 22 months, and $1,209 in interest.
lines.say: Stay on the twenty-four percent card, paying the same two eighty-seven: twenty-two months, and twelve oh nine in interest.

lines.cap: The transfer: 18 months, and just the $150 fee. About $1,059 saved.
lines.say: The transfer: eighteen months, and just the hundred fifty dollar fee. About a thousand dollars saved.
Now, how it goes wrong.

scene.label: Paying only $150 a month on the transfer
scene.sub: still owed when the 0% promo ends

lines.cap: Pay only $150 a month, and when the promo ends, $2,450 is still there, back at full interest.
lines.say: Pay only a hundred fifty a month, and when the promo ends, twenty-four fifty is still there, back at full interest.

scene.head: BEFORE YOU TRANSFER
items: Can you clear it before the promo ends?
Is the fee less than the interest you'd pay?
Will you stop using the old card?

lines.say: So before you transfer, ask four questions.
Can you pay it off before the promo ends? Divide by the months, and check.
Is the fee smaller than the interest you'd pay otherwise?
Will you stop using the old card? Moving the debt, then filling the old card back up, doubles it.

lines.cap: And read the terms. On many cards, a late payment can end the 0% early, and new purchases may not get the promo rate.
lines.say: And read the terms. On many cards, a late payment can end the zero percent early, and new purchases may not get the promo rate.

scene.text: A transfer buys time. It doesn't pay the debt.

lines.say: A balance transfer buys you time. It doesn't pay the debt. The plan still has to.
